 Digital Pressure Gauge: 6 Smart Steps for Reliable Readings
 A digital pressure gauge replaces the Bourdon tube, gears and pointer with a silicon sensor, a converter and a clear numeric display. Used correctly, it becomes a dependable field instrument and a portable reference for checking other gauges.
 Piezoresistive Sensor 
 Accuracy in % FS

 Test Gauge Use 
 Electronic gauges read pressure as numbers, not pointer angles, so parallax and pointer friction disappear. This guide explains how a digital pressure gauge works, how to read its accuracy and how to use it as a reference.
 Hello everyone, today we are going to learn how a digital pressure gauge works, how to read its accuracy specification and how to use it correctly in the field and in calibration.
 What Is a Digital Pressure Gauge?
 A digital pressure gauge is a self contained instrument that senses process pressure with an electronic sensor and shows the value as numbers on an LCD or LED display. It does the same job as a mechanical Bourdon tube pressure gauge , but without any moving parts in the measuring path.
 Inside the case sit a pressure sensor, an amplifier, an analog to digital converter, a microcontroller and a display. Most models use the silicon sensing element explained in piezoresistive vs capacitive pressure sensors , because it is robust, small and lower in cost.
 Image credit: Tameson . Image courtesy of Tameson, shown here for educational reference. 
 Engineers in Indian plants meet these gauges in three roles: as permanent process indicators, as portable test gauges for calibration, and as data loggers for pressure tests. The basic choice between electronic and mechanical sensing is discussed in electronic vs mechanical pressure sensors .
 Advertisement 
 How the Gauge Turns Pressure Into Numbers
 The process pressure acts on a thin diaphragm, usually stainless steel in front of a silicon chip, with silicone oil carrying the pressure between them. The silicon chip has four resistors diffused into it, connected as a bridge.
 When the diaphragm bends, two resistors are stretched and two are compressed, so their resistance changes in opposite directions. The bridge, the same circuit described in Wheatstone bridge applications , converts this tiny change into a millivolt output proportional to pressure.
 Diaphragm Pressure bends the isolating diaphragm
 Bridge Piezoresistors give a millivolt signal
 Amplifier Signal is raised to converter level
 ADC Analog value becomes a digital count
 Processor Linearisation and temperature correction
 Display Pressure shown in the chosen unit
 An amplifier raises the millivolt signal, and an analog to digital converter turns it into a number, as explained in analog to digital conversion . The microcontroller then applies stored correction tables for non linearity and temperature, which is why a good electronic gauge holds its accuracy across a wide ambient range.
 Do You Know?
 Silicon piezoresistors change resistance far more strongly with strain than metal foil gauges do. That higher sensitivity is why a tiny silicon chip can resolve pressure changes of a few parts in ten thousand.
 Accuracy, Resolution and Range Explained
 Accuracy of a digital pressure gauge is normally stated as a percentage of full scale, written % FS. A 0 to 25 bar gauge with 0.05 % FS accuracy may be wrong by plus or minus 0.0125 bar anywhere in its range, the same idea as the classes in pressure gauge accuracy classes .
 Some premium gauges quote accuracy as a percentage of reading, or as a combination of reading and full scale. Ralston Instruments points out that two gauges can only be compared fairly when their accuracy is stated the same way and their ranges match.
 Resolution is the smallest digit the display shows, and it is not the same as accuracy. ICS Schneider Messtechnik notes that a gauge showing 10.000 bar may still carry a permissible deviation of plus or minus 0.050 bar, a point covered well in accuracy vs precision .
 0.25 % FS WIKA CPG500 accuracy 
 10 ms CPG500 measuring rate 
 1500 h CPG500 battery life, 2 AA cells 
 4 : 1 Minimum reference ratio 
 WIKA specifies its CPG500 basic digital pressure gauge at 0.25 % FS plus or minus 1 digit, with a measuring rate of 10 ms, which means 100 readings per second. Its eight ranges run from minus 1 to 16 bar up to 0 to 1000 bar, and two AA cells last about 1500 hours.
 Quick Tip
 Always choose the smallest range that still covers your maximum test pressure. A percentage of full scale error becomes a large absolute error when a 250 bar gauge is used to check a 10 bar instrument.
 Reference Error and Test Accuracy Ratio Formula
 When a digital pressure gauge serves as a reference, its absolute error must be much smaller than the tolerance of the device under test. ICS Schneider recommends a test accuracy ratio of at least 4 : 1, the same principle discussed in measurement uncertainty in calibration .
 Reference error = Full scale × Accuracy % ÷ 100 
 Device tolerance = Device span × Class % ÷ 100 
 TAR = Device tolerance ÷ Reference error 
Example:
Reference gauge 0 to 25 bar, 0.05 % FS
Reference error = 25 × 0.05 ÷ 100 = 0.0125 bar
Device under test 0 to 10 bar, class 1.0
Device tolerance = 10 × 1.0 ÷ 100 = 0.100 bar
 TAR = 0.100 ÷ 0.0125 = 8.0 : 1, acceptable 
 The ratio of 8 : 1 comfortably beats the 4 : 1 minimum, so the reference contributes little to the result. If the ratio falls below 4 : 1, pick a better reference or a smaller range before you sign any certificate.

 Second Worked Example: Wrong Range Choice
 Suppose the same 0.05 % FS accuracy is bought in a 0 to 250 bar range and used to check the same 10 bar class 1.0 gauge. The reference error becomes 250 × 0.05 ÷ 100 = 0.125 bar, which is larger than the 0.100 bar tolerance being tested.
 The ratio is now 0.100 ÷ 0.125 = 0.8 : 1, so the check is meaningless even though the reference has a fine percentage figure. ICS Schneider uses exactly this comparison to show that range selection matters as much as the accuracy class.
 Power Options and Output Types
 Battery Powered
 Runs on AA, AAA or coin cells with auto power off to stretch life.
 Best for: portable test gauges and remote points
 Portable 
 Loop Powered
 Draws power from a 4 to 20 mA loop and shows the local value.
 Best for: retrofit displays on transmitter loops
 No battery 
 Externally Powered With Output
 24 V DC supply with analog output or switch contacts.
 Best for: panel and skid indication with alarms
 Output 
 Logging Gauge
 Stores readings with time stamps for later download.
 Best for: hydro tests and leak tests
 Data 
 Battery models suit test benches and remote points where no power is wired, and Tameson notes they keep reading during a power outage. Loop powered versions sit inside a 4 to 20 mA current loop and take their energy from the loop current itself.
 Gauges with outputs blur the line between gauge and transmitter, so it helps to understand the difference covered in pressure gauge vs pressure transmitter . For hazardous areas, check the Ex marking and the battery type allowed by the certificate, as explained in explosion proof vs intrinsically safe instruments .
 Do You Know?
 A logging digital pressure gauge can replace a paper chart recorder during a pipeline hydro test. The stored file shows every reading with its time, which makes the test record far easier to review and archive.
 Digital Versus Analog Gauge in the Field
 Feature Digital Gauge Analog Bourdon Gauge 
 Sensing Silicon or thin film sensor Bourdon tube, linkage, pointer 
 Typical accuracy 0.025 to 0.5 % FS 0.5 to 2.5 % of span 
 Reading Numeric, no parallax Pointer on dial, parallax possible 
 Power Battery, loop or supply None needed 
 Extra features Min and max, tare, logging, units None 
 Pulsation Damping filter in firmware Needs liquid fill or snubber 
 Ralston Instruments notes that the Bourdon tube design dates from 1849 and has served for over 170 years. Mechanical gauges still win where no power is acceptable and only an occasional glance is needed, while the digital type wins wherever accuracy, recording and unit flexibility matter, as weighed in pressure gauge selection factors .
 Myth: More digits on the display means more accuracy.
 Fact: Resolution only shows the smallest step, while accuracy comes from the sensor and its calibration.
 Myth: A digital gauge never needs calibration.
 Fact: Sensors drift with time, overpressure and temperature cycling, so a fixed calibration interval still applies.
 Myth: Any 0.05 % gauge is a good reference.
 Fact: A high range turns 0.05 % FS into a large absolute error, so match the range to the test.
 Myth: Digital gauges cannot handle pulsation.
 Fact: Firmware damping and a snubber give a steady reading on pump discharge lines.
 6 Smart Steps to Use a Digital Pressure Gauge as a Test Gauge
 1
 Check Status
 Confirm the calibration certificate is valid and the battery is healthy.
 2
 Pick Range
 Use a range that gives a test accuracy ratio of 4 : 1 or better.
 3
 Zero at Rest
 Vent to atmosphere and use the zero function before connecting.
 4
 Connect Safely
 Use correct fittings, sealing and an isolation and vent valve.
 5
 Stabilise
 Wait for temperature and pressure to settle at each point.
 6
 Record Both Ways
 Read 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 % rising and falling.
 The five point rising and falling sequence matches the procedure described by ICS Schneider and catches both error and hysteresis. A dead weight tester or a multifunction process calibrator can generate the pressure, while the gauge acts as the reading standard.
 Quick Tip
 Zero a gauge pressure model only when it is open to atmosphere, never while connected to a live line. A false zero adds a fixed offset to every point you record afterwards.
 Selection Checklist for Indian Plants
 Range about 1.5 to 2 times the normal working pressure
 Accuracy class and whether it is % FS or % of reading
 Gauge, absolute or compound reference
 Wetted material suited to the process medium
 Process connection, often half inch NPT or G half inch
 IP rating for outdoor monsoon conditions
 Battery life, loop power or external supply
 Ex certification for hazardous zones
 Logging, units and peak hold features needed
 Ask the supplier whether readings are gauge or absolute, since the difference explained in absolute vs gauge pressure is a common source of 1 bar errors. Also confirm the overload rating, and add protection as described in pressure gauge over range protection where spikes are likely.
 Advantages
 No parallax and easy numeric reading
 Higher accuracy than most mechanical gauges
 Peak hold, tare, unit switching and logging
 No pointer flutter thanks to digital damping
 Ideal portable reference for calibration
 Limitations
 Needs batteries or an external supply
 Higher purchase cost than a dial gauge
 Display can be hard to read in direct sunlight
 Hazardous areas need certified versions
 Electronics can be damaged by severe surges

 Installation and Troubleshooting Tips
 Mount the gauge so the display faces the operator and the sensor is not exposed to radiant heat. On steam lines use a siphon , and on pump discharge add a pressure snubber so spikes do not overload the diaphragm.
 A reading that creeps upward in sunlight usually points to a temperature effect rather than real pressure, the same issue seen in pressure transmitter temperature effects . Water hammer can also cause a permanent zero shift, as discussed in hammer effect in pressure gauges .

 Digital Pressure Gauge FAQ
 How does a digital pressure gauge work?
 Pressure bends a diaphragm that strains piezoresistors arranged in a bridge on a silicon chip. The bridge then produces a small millivolt signal that changes in direct proportion to the applied pressure.
 An amplifier and converter turn that voltage into a number. The processor corrects it for temperature and non linearity and shows it on the display.
 What does 0.05 % FS accuracy mean?
 It means the error can be up to 0.05 percent of the full scale value at any point in the range. On a 25 bar gauge that is plus or minus 0.0125 bar.
 The same error applies at low readings, so the percentage of reading gets worse near zero. Choose the smallest suitable range to keep that error small.
 Is resolution the same as accuracy?
 No, resolution is only the smallest step the display can show. A gauge can show three decimal places and still be wrong in the second decimal.
 Accuracy comes from the sensor, the electronics and the quality of the last calibration. Always read the accuracy statement on the data sheet rather than counting digits on the display.
 What test accuracy ratio should I use?
 A common rule is that the reference should be at least four times more accurate than the device under test. ICS Schneider recommends this 4 : 1 minimum for gauge checks.
 Higher ratios such as 10 : 1 are even better when available. Below 4 : 1, the reference error becomes a large part of the result.
